Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Consumer Goods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register and then press the star key followed by the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Consumer Goods' Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Jordan Hayes, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Torres, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hayes.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Apex Consumer Goods delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, sales performance and channel strategy, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.45 billion, representing a 6.2% increase compared to the prior year, or 6.8% on an organic basis. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by pricing realization, supply chain productivity savings, and favorable input costs. Operating income was $760 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.28. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me provide more color on these results and tie them into our key metrics. Starting with organic sales growth, which hit 6.8% in Q3, accelerating from prior quarters and outpacing the industry average of around 4.2% according to NielsenIQ. This broke down to 2.5 points from pricing actions, roughly 3 points from volume and mix improvements, and the rest from resilient category trends. Volume turned positive at 2.1% overall, our first uptick in several quarters, driven by household penetration gains and faster velocity in power brands. In snacks and confectionery, which make up 28% of sales, we saw 7.8% organic growth from health-focused items like protein bars and plant-based gummies, gaining significant market share against bigger players through expanded distribution in club stores.

Price and mix added 3.1 points, with targeted hikes of 4-6% on essentials balanced by promotions on value packs. Premiumization played a big role, with consumers shifting to eco-friendly personal care lines that grew double digits. Regionally, North America led at 6.4% organic, boosted by e-commerce now at 18% of sales there; EMEA was 4.2% with steady pricing; Latin America surged 8.1% on volume recovery; and APAC was softer at 1.9% but stabilizing with tailored innovations.

On pricing actions specifically, we took measured increases averaging 7.1% year-over-year, down from higher levels earlier as inflation eases. This was precise: 8-12% on loyal power brands like nutribars and wipes, 5-7% on beverages, and 6.2% on personal care, backed by AI elasticity modeling that kept us within safe ranges. Pricing drove 6.3 points of growth, offsetting 2.1-point volume softness mainly in impulse categories, for net 4.2% organic in some segments—but overall it was stronger. North America saw the biggest lift at 8.5% pricing with minimal erosion, while Europe was more challenged but countered with packs. This discipline added 75 basis points to sequential gross margin and affirmed our brand strength.

Gross margin reached 48.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 50 sequentially, beating our guide thanks to 180 bps from price/mix, 90 bps from productivity, and 70 bps from easing inputs like dairy down 8% and wheat 6%. FX hurt 110 bps, but we offset with network shifts like closing Midwest plants. North America hit 47.8%, LatAm 42.5% despite inflation. We're guiding Q4 to 45.5-46.0%, targeting 48% by 2025 via portfolio focus and zero-based savings.

Supply chain efficiencies were pivotal, generating $285 million in gross savings, up 22%, fueling 180 bps of margin expansion and countering 4.2% input inflation. Procurement was 42% at $120 million via supplier consolidation and sustainable sourcing like 35% regenerative palm oil. Manufacturing added $80 million with cobots cutting cycle times 18%, OTIF at 98.2%. Logistics saved $63 million on optimized routes, nearshoring to Mexico/Vietnam. Inventory optimization freed $450 million working capital. North America led savings, with $750 million transformation ahead including blockchain traceability.

Market share trends reinforce this: up 110 bps overall for our eighth straight quarter, tracked via Nielsen/IRI. Beverages +1.8% to 22.4%, snacks +1.4% to 19.7% with savory at 24.5%, beauty/personal +0.9%, household +0.7%. North America +140 bps, Europe +80 bps on discounter wins, APAC +1.2% via digital, LatAm +90 bps. Driven by AI optimization, channel mastery like 98% Amazon ACV, and NPD focus.

Turning to key strategic priorities, our four pillars—portfolio optimization, sustainable innovation, digital acceleration, supply chain resilience—delivered this. We rationalized 15% low-velocity SKUs, freeing $250 million SG&A; premium now 42% of portfolio. Sustainability hit 85% recyclable packaging, 92% sustainable ag; ESG boosted NPS to +62. Digital e-comm at 28%, AI personalization up repeat rates 22%. Emerging markets 32% of sales, 11% growth. Raising FY24 organic to 5.5-6.5%, Q4 4-5.5%, FY25 5-7%, with pricing 1-2%, volume 2.5-4 points, led by NA 5-7%, APAC/LatAm 6-8%.

Next, Lisa Chen will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across all our channels, especially with our new "Live Vibrant" campaign, which leverages consumer insights to highlight health and sustainability. This has driven trial rates up 20% in key categories and supported premium mix shifts.

Following me, Mike Torres will discuss supply chain performance.

Mike Torres:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. Building on Sarah's points, our Factory 4.0 initiatives with cobots and predictive maintenance have boosted productivity across plants, while nearshoring reduces risks. We are also focused on reducing our carbon footprint, with Scope 1 and 2 emissions down 18% year-over-year through solar and regenerative sourcing.

After me, Dr. Elena Vasquez will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Innovation is central to our growth, complementing the new launches I'll touch on later. Our R&D investments, up 18% to $320 million, focus on platforms like functional beverages and clean beauty. Recent efforts in precision nutrition and microbiome tech are yielding high margins and consumer loyalty.

Finally, Tom Reilly will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Elena. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving our sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel, now 28% of sales, and we are also investing in our retail partnerships, gaining ACV in club, mass, and emerging digital like TikTok Shop. Market share gains in key regions stem from velocity programs and omnichannel households growing 19%.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Tom. Before we open the line for questions, I'd like to spend a few minutes on one of our key growth engines: new product launches and our innovation pipeline. As you know, in the CPG space, innovation is the lifeblood of sustaining category growth amid softening volumes in legacy staples and shifting consumer preferences toward health, sustainability, and convenience. Our disciplined approach—rooted in consumer insights from our proprietary VitalVoice panel of 50,000+ households globally—has delivered outsized returns, with new products accounting for 28% of our Q3 net sales, up from 22% a year ago. This outperforms the industry average of 15-20% as reported in recent IRI and Nielsen data.

Recent launches have generated $450 million in incremental sales since rollouts, a 12% velocity lift. Leading is VitaGlow Hydration+ in functional beverages, launched Q2 in North America—five SKUs with 50% less sugar, sea mineral electrolytes, ashwagandha. Captured 8.2% share in enhanced water per IRI, 4.1% penetration double benchmarks, 65% grocery ACV, 45% convenience, 35% repeat rate, 42% gross margins via co-manufacturing.

EarthPure Home Care in Europe/APAC responds to premiumization, plant-derived cleaners free of phosphates/parabens/microplastics, 25% trial in UK/Germany, 18% velocity vs. legacy, 32% e-comm, recyclable PCR bottles earning 4.8 stars, NPS +22, 3 points category growth in EMEA amid PFAS bans.

In snacks, NutriBurst Protein Clusters—15g protein, upcycled ingredients—DTC first, $120 million run-rate, 55% margins via Singapore fermentation, 4.2x digital ROI, 12% share 18-34s per Kantar.

Pipeline robustest in five years, 35 SKUs, 40% platforms, 30% regional, 30% adjacencies. Near-term: FlexiFuel Energy Shots Q4'24-Q1'25, nootropics for $4B segment, 28% preference Brazil pilots, $200M year-one. Mid-term H1'25: BioAdapt Skincare, probiotic creams, 5% clean beauty share, AI personalization 20% LTV lift. Long-term: GeneFit Meal Kits, DNA-customized, 40% adherence vs. HelloFresh.

NA 65% new sales +14%, Europe 22% +2.5 share sustainability, APAC 45% velocity. Pillars: sustainable sourcing 90% RSPO, omnichannel 50% digital FY26, AI agility 24-to-14 month cycles. Positions for 8-10% FY25 organic vs. 4-5% industry.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions as before. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morningstar.

David Lee:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, David. Sustainability is embedded in our strategy. As Sarah and Mike noted, 85% recyclable packaging, 92% sustainable cocoa/palm via Rainforest Alliance, and initiatives like Green Apex with bio-detergents and zero-waste pouches driving 12% growth in EMEA. New launches like EarthPure use biodegradable formulas and PCR bottles, boosting NPS. We're on track for Scope 1/2 carbon neutrality by 2030, emissions down 18%, securing green financing. This meets consumer demand—35% wallet share eco-focused—and regulatory like EU Green Deal.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays.

Maria Gonzalez:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Tom Reilly:
Thanks, Maria. Emerging markets are key, now 32% sales targeting 40% by 2026. APAC/LatAm posted 11% organic Q3, with 9% in China via WeChat for hydration, Vietnam nearshoring. Brazil yogurt +0.8 vs. Nestle, India/Indonesia affordable sachets 25% mass penetration. China+1 shifts cut lead times 22%, e-comm 45% FMCG there. FY25 guide 6-8% growth there via listings, bodega expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with Goldman Sachs.

Robert Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Sarah Jenkins:
Sure, Robert. Inflation easing to mid-single digits lets us moderate pricing to 1-2% FY25, after 7.1% Q3 that drove growth without much erosion—elasticity -1.1. Premium mix +3 points offsets downtrading, affordable premium like value HydratePro mitigates. Volumes positive on innovation, share gains. Gross margin resilient at 48.2%, hedged inputs, productivity covers residuals.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

Mike Torres:
Emily, AI is transformative. Demand sensing with Palantir/Blue Yonder cuts forecast error 25%, stockouts 22%, turns 8.5x. Dynamic pricing SAP S/4HANA real-time elasticity. Route Optimizer Google Cloud saves 12% freight. Yield tracking Predix 92% failure prediction. $750M transformation, blockchain IBM pilots. Delivered $285M Q3 savings, $350M FY25 expected.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jordan Hayes for closing remarks.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders, backed by our innovation pipeline, margin discipline, and strategic execution. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex Consumer Goods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
